Create an Audited Refit Function for Distance-Removal Models

Source: R/gdr_refitter.R
make_gdr_refitter.Rd

Build a refit function for multiScale_optim(refit_fn = ...) that refits an unmarked distance-removal (GDR) model at each candidate scale of effect from its original estimates and from extra starting values you declare. It keeps the best clean fit and writes a record of every attempt to an audit directory. A distance-removal likelihood can have more than one local optimum, and several starts make it less likely that a poor optimum is accepted unnoticed.

Usage

make_gdr_refitter(
  model,
  cold_starts,
  audit_dir,
  provenance = list(),
  tmb_settings = NULL
)

Arguments

model

The starting model. One of:

  • an unmarkedFitGDR fitted by unmarked::gdistremoval() with engine = "C";

  • an unmarkedFitGDR fitted with engine = "TMB", including models with random intercepts;

  • an unmarkedFitGDRField from fit_gdr_response_field().

The refit function is tied to this model. It reuses the model's data, formulas, cutoff K, mixture, distance function, output units and optimizer settings, and it never switches engine. The model needs unmarked 1.5.2, plus TMB 1.9.25 for the TMB engine. Formulas with offset() terms and zero-inflated TMB models (mixture = "ZIP" with engine = "TMB") are not supported.

cold_starts

Named list of one or more extra starting vectors on the link scales of the model, for example list(cold = cold). For a C-engine model, name each vector exactly like unmarked::coef(model), such as "lambda(Int)" and "dist(Int)". For a TMB-engine or field model, supply one value for every fixed coefficient and log SD, either unnamed in the order of gdr_start_values(model)$starts, or named by parameter block and position, such as "beta_lambda[1]" or "lsigma_lambda[1]". Random effects are not included. Each vector must differ from the model's estimates and from the other vectors, and the names "original" and "final" are reserved. These values are model coefficients, not kernel scales of effect and not the cutoff K.

audit_dir

Character string naming the directory for audit records. It must be new or empty, and it is created if needed. (For a field model, an existing directory with records is also accepted.) Keep it, because the records are the only trace of failed attempts. See "Read the audit directory".

provenance

Optional named list of your own identifiers, such as a data source, a script version or an archive DOI. Use simple values: atomic vectors of at most 64 elements, or nested lists of them, with at most 64 KiB in total. It is copied into every record as supplied and is not checked.

tmb_settings

For a TMB-engine or field model, a named list of the optimizer settings to use for every refit. Leave it NULL (the default) for a C-engine model, whose settings are read from the fitted model. Required elements:

  • method: one of "BFGS", "Nelder-Mead", "CG" or "L-BFGS-B".

  • se: logical. Whether the final refit of each call computes standard errors.

  • threads: must be 1.

  • control: named list of finite numeric optim() controls with a positive integer maxit, such as list(maxit = 2000L, reltol = 1e-10).

Optional elements:

  • lower, upper: parameter bounds for method = "L-BFGS-B", either one number or one value per coordinate in the fitted optimizer order (names(gdr_start_values(model)$fitted_values)), which can differ from the start order.

  • random.start: how TMB starts each search for the random-effect values. "cached_best" (the TMB default) starts from the best values found so far. "zero" starts from zero.

  • inner.control: a list with positive maxit, tol, grad.tol and step.tol for that inner search.

  • record_memory: TRUE records the memory used by the R process at each phase of a fit. It requires the ps package. The default is FALSE.

For a field model, pass the identical list used in fit_gdr_response_field().

Value

A function with arguments model, data and context, for the refit_fn argument of multiScale_optim(). The optimizer calls it with the starting model, a copy of its frame in which the kernel-weighted covariates have new values, and a context whose covs element names those columns. Each call returns one fitted model of the same class as model, with an attribute msr_gdr_refit_audit that summarizes the call:

  • status: "returned" for a successful call.

  • attempts: one record per start ("original", each cold start, and "final"), each with the start, converged, the logLik, coefficients on the link scale, warnings, any error, the covariance status, whether it was eligible, and the optimizer output (par, value, counts, convergence, message). TMB attempts add marginal_score (largest absolute gradient, its 0.001 threshold and whether it passed) and optimizer_point_file.

  • selected: the index of the start with the highest log-likelihood.

  • objective_only: TRUE when the call skipped the final refit.

  • contract_sha256 and input_context_sha256: fingerprints that tie the call to contract.rds and to the inputs it received. path is the summary record.

A field model returns the record described in fit_gdr_response_field() instead. A failed call stops with an error of class msr_gdr_refit_error, whose audit and audit_file elements hold the record and its path.

How each refit works

At every call the function fits the model from its original estimates (the start named "original") and from each cold start, then keeps the start with the highest finite log-likelihood. That start must be eligible: converged (code 0) with no warnings and, for TMB models, usable covariance and a largest absolute gradient below 0.001. If it is not eligible, the call fails rather than returning a lower-likelihood fit in its place.

When multiScale_optim() needs the fitted model rather than only its likelihood, a final fit starts from the selected coefficients with the original standard-error request. It must also be eligible and may lose no more than 1e-5 log-likelihood units. C-engine intermediate fits skip coefficient Hessians, which saves time.

Only the columns named in context$covs may change between calls, and only static site covariates qualify. A covariate whose name also appears in the yearly or observation covariates is rejected, so give it a distinct name. Changes to the counts, the other covariates, the survey protocol or the row order stop the call.

Each TMB attempt builds a new TMB objective and starts its random effects at zero. It always runs TMB::sdreport(), even with se = FALSE, so TMB refits are not faster without standard errors. Usable covariance requires a positive-definite Hessian, fixed covariance and joint precision. The random effects must sit at a mode with positive-definite curvature and a largest gradient and Newton decrement below 0.001. The objective, recomputed at the optimizer's coordinates, must also agree with the reported value within 1e-7. These are local checks. They do not show that the mode is unique or that TMB's Laplace approximation is accurate.

Declare TMB settings

A C-engine fit keeps the optimizer settings it used, so they are read automatically. A TMB fit in unmarked 1.5.2 does not keep them, and its constructor does not pass optimizer controls through. Declare them in tmb_settings instead. The refit function passes them to optim() directly, without changing unmarked. A typical list is:

list(method = "BFGS", se = TRUE, threads = 1L,
     control = list(maxit = 2500L, reltol = 1e-10))

random.start and inner.control change how TMB searches for the random effects. A different setting can reach a different numerical solution, so treat a change as a new analysis and check its results. No setting is changed automatically after a failure. With record_memory = TRUE, each phase record stores the resident memory of the whole R process and its lifetime peak, in bytes. These numbers include everything else loaded in the session, so they are not the memory used by one phase.

Read the audit directory

FileWrittenContents
contract.rdsWhen the refit function is createdFingerprints of the original data and design, the settings, the starts, the original coefficients and optimizer summary, and the identity of unmarked, TMB and multiScaleR, with a SHA-256 of the whole contract
refit-*-request.rdsAt the start of each callThe call's opening record
refit-*-input.rdsAfter the inputs pass their checksFingerprints of the new data and the changed columns
refit-*-attempt-*-request.rdsBefore each start enters unmarkedThe start and its name
refit-*-attempt-*-point.rdsTMB only, after optimization and before covarianceThe optimizer result
refit-*-attempt-*.rdsAfter each startThe completed attempt record
refit-*.rdsAt the end of each callThe summary, also attached to the returned model

A request without a matching completed record documents an attempt that never finished, for example after an interruption. Keep it. Records contain numbers, settings and SHA-256 fingerprints. They contain no raw data, design matrices, Hessians or fitted models, so they stay small.

The optimizer point file (class msr_gdr_optimizer_point) is written before the covariance step, so a later covariance failure still leaves evidence that the optimization finished. It holds the optimizer's par, value, counts, convergence and message, the coordinate labels, data and layout fingerprints, the cutoff K, the declared settings and the elapsed time of each phase. It is always marked inference_eligible = FALSE. It is not a fitted model, it gives no standard errors, and a fit cannot be resumed from it.

At each call the refit function also confirms that unmarked, TMB and this function's own code have not changed since it was created. A change, including a different installation in a new worker process, stops the call before fitting.

Refit a response field

For a model from fit_gdr_response_field(), each call refits the field with all of that function's checks, with the range held fixed. Use the same cold_starts and the identical tmb_settings, and run multiScale_optim() with n_cores = 1. The ordinary update() method stops for field models, so this refit function is the way to refit one.

What the checks do not establish

Coefficient standard errors from the returned model treat the selected scales of effect as known. The function adds no priors, bootstrap intervals or kernel-scale uncertainty. Agreement among the declared starts does not guarantee that a better optimum does not exist elsewhere.

The cutoff K (the largest abundance the likelihood considers at a point) is unrelated to the K column of aic_tab(), which counts parameters. Reusing one cutoff does not replace a check that results are insensitive to it.

See the "Refit from several starting values" section of vignette("v12-distance-removal", package = "multiScaleR") for a worked example.

See also

multiScale_optim(), gdr_start_values(), fit_gdr_response_field(), validate_unmarked_data(), aic_tab()

Examples

if (as.character(utils::packageVersion("unmarked")) == "1.5.2") {
  # Five point counts: birds by distance band and by time interval
  yd <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(1, 0), c(0, 2), c(2, 1), c(0, 0))
  yr <- rbind(c(0, 0, 0), c(0, 1, 0), c(1, 0, 1), c(1, 1, 1), c(0, 0, 0))
  frame <- unmarked::unmarkedFrameGDR(yd, yr, dist.breaks = c(0, 25, 75),
    unitsIn = "m", period.lengths = c(1, 2, 1),
    siteCovs = data.frame(hab = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 5)))
  # Fit the starting model (C engine) before declaring extra starts
  model <- unmarked::gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~hab, data = frame,
    output = "abund", K = 40, se = FALSE, engine = "C",
    starts = c(log(8), 0, log(40), qlogis(0.3)), control = list(maxit = 2000))
  # One extra start, named like the model coefficients (link scales)
  cold <- unmarked::coef(model)
  cold[] <- 0
  cold["dist(Int)"] <- log(30)
  audit_dir <- tempfile("msr-gdr-audit-")
  refit <- make_gdr_refitter(model, list(cold = cold), audit_dir = audit_dir)

  # multiScale_optim() calls refit() at each candidate scale. Calling it
  # once here, on the original data, shows what each call records.
  fit <- refit(model, frame, context = list(covs = "hab"))
  audit <- attr(fit, "msr_gdr_refit_audit")
  # Log-likelihood and eligibility of each start, then the selected start
  print(sapply(audit$attempts, function(a)
    c(logLik = a$logLik, eligible = a$eligible)))
  print(audit$attempts[[audit$selected]]$name)
  # contract.rds, plus request, input, attempt and summary records
  print(list.files(audit_dir))
}
#>               [,1]      [,2]      [,3]
#> logLik   -14.77773 -14.77773 -14.77773
#> eligible   1.00000   1.00000   1.00000
#> [1] "original"
#>  [1] "contract.rds"                                           
#>  [2] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-1-request.rds"
#>  [3] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-1.rds"        
#>  [4] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-2-request.rds"
#>  [5] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-2.rds"        
#>  [6] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-3-request.rds"
#>  [7] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-attempt-3.rds"        
#>  [8] "refit-7970-20261117221256687209-1-input.rds"
